chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about renting land for food (grain), and he said, 'If it is from its own food (grain), there is no good in it.'

key_terms.فَلَا خَيْرَ فِيهِ: There is no good in it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying land rent with the crop produced from that land?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the prohibition of paying land rent with grain from the same crop highlights the principle of avoiding uncertainty (gharar) and ensuring distinct value in agricultural partnerships. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing valid muzara'ah from invalid forms where the return is indistinguishable from the input, reflecting the broader Islamic economic emphasis on fair exchange and risk mitigation.
